---
title: "Rust implementation and reuse"
---

## Architecture {#sec-implementation}

The numerical library is independent of the web page. Its FFT, initial-condition, growth, nLPT, sheet, and geometric-clipping modules originate in the MIT-licensed Hopf–Cole cosmology core. The source revision is recorded in [the decisions log](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/decisions.md), and the original copyright is retained. The historical Rust crate name `hcc_core` is preserved for compatibility with the inherited tests and API links.

The new modules add cosmological PM evolution, initial-field and trajectory tangents, conservative sheet observables, and a checked laboratory request/response facade. The geometry visitor supplies the same periodic connectivity to Jacobian checks and continuous mode integration. This prevents a plotting mesh from silently differing from the sheet whose mass is measured.

| Layer | Responsibility | Reuse boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Grid and FFT | Periodic indexing, transforms, spectral operators | Standalone fields on 1D–3D grids |
| Growth and nLPT | Spatial recurrence and time factors | Fixed input modes, cosmology, perturbative order |
| Sheet and R3D | Conservative overlap integrals | Supplied unwrapped positions and optional P1 weights |
| Observables | Interval deposition, PDF measures, fixed-mass modes | Independent of how trajectories were generated |
| PM and tangents | Discrete cosmological evolution and JVPs | Supplied initial positions, momenta, directions |
| Laboratory facade | Validate inputs, report orientation, serialize reproducible results | Native Rust and Wasm use the same function |
| Browser worker | Own Wasm/GPU backends, serialize work and cancel obsolete requests | Shared trajectories and separately validated continuous observables |

## Build and inspect

Install Rust, the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target, wasm-pack, Python 3, and Quarto. From a checkout:

```sh
make test
make wasm
make api
make check
make site
python3 scripts/serve.py 8790 _site
```

`make test` runs native numerical and frontend contract tests. `make test-wasm` checks the generated binary in Node after `make wasm`; the browser self-check exercises its worker integration. `make wasm` writes the browser package into `app/pkg/`; `make api` publishes rustdoc into `api/`. The provenance checker resolves each equation's function link, each test badge, and each lab hash key. Quarto copies the standalone app, packaged data, and API documentation into the rendered book.

Open [the API reference](../api/hcc_core/index.html) for types, argument conventions, and implementation details. These pages are generated from the actual source used by the lab. A new project can depend on `core/` with a Cargo path dependency and use the same routines without Quarto or a browser.

```toml
[dependencies]
hcc-core = { path = "../precrossedsheet/core" }
```

```rust
use hcc_core::{Cosmo, ics::Preset};
let mut sim = Cosmo::new(2, 24, 1.0);
sim.keep_tensors = Some(true);
sim.set_ic_preset(Preset::PlaneWaves {
    modes: vec![([1, 0, 0], 0.3, 0.0), ([0, 1, 0], 0.2, 0.4)]
}, 0.0, 0.0);
sim.build_lpt(4);
let d = 0.4 * sim.shell_crossing(4);
assert!(sim.lpt_ref().min_jacobian(d, 4) > 0.0);
let density = sim.sheet_density_exact(d, 4, 32, false, 1e4);
```

For production use also check the affine simplex orientations and the resolution dependence. The high-level laboratory facade performs these checks automatically, but direct low-level callers remain responsible for input dimensions, field lengths, and validity.

## Numerical limits and derivative scope

In the CPU reference, inherited LPT spatial fields and deposited density arrays use `f32`; Fourier arithmetic, clipping moments, PM state, and analytic tangent arithmetic use `f64`. The optional resident PM stage uses `f32` state and tangent arithmetic, as detailed in @sec-gpu-pm. A finite-difference check must choose its step above representation noise and below nonlinear truncation error. The facade bounds allocations before building the field, and requires a conservative Gaussian input bandwidth. The recorded native benchmarks distinguish measured peak RSS from the conservative memory estimate.

The differentiable route carries an initial-condition JVP through nLPT, or supplied phase-space directions through PM, to continuous P0 Fourier modes and power. It supports directional derivatives at fixed cosmology and clocks. It does not provide cosmological growth derivatives, a reverse-mode adjoint, or exact-clipped-density shape derivatives. Those are separate implementation tasks; they should not be implied by the word “differentiable.”

The browser uses Wasm and Canvas2D/SVG as the portable capability tier, with optional checked GPU PM evolution and continuous-mode observations described below. The worker keeps large calculations off the page thread; the resource envelope permits lattice 64³ and observation/force grids up to 128³ when their combined estimate fits 1 GiB, while 1D and 2D ceilings are 1024 and 256². Invalid requests return explicit errors without replacing the requested grid. The same low-level Rust library supports caller-managed larger allocations outside the facade. The facade intentionally uses the same limits in native and Wasm runs so one manifest denotes one experiment.

## Data lineage and adaptation

The geometric example in @sec-two-point-example runs directly in the chapter browser: periodic interval overlaps supply its correlation and joint pair tables. It uses four fixed masses on a unit circle, with explicit interval lengths and arrangement. Its query-string permalink and CSV preserve those inputs. This small analytic experiment has independent native overlap, spatial-quadrature and Fourier-window tests; it does not invoke a cosmological trajectory or add a general two-point observable to the Wasm facade. Its pure functions can be reused from [the widget module](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/app/js/two-point.js), while the continuum correlation of a general sheet follows from its continuous Fourier modes as derived in @sec-two-point-power.

The archival replay consists of extracted summary arrays, not entire simulation snapshots. Its manifest records repository, revision, source paths, checksums, and the extraction recipe. To substitute another dataset, preserve the estimator, filter, normalization, weighting, epoch, and crossing metadata. The original archival PDF histograms are conditional on their finite display range and do not report retained tail probabilities; the live PDF histograms preserve those probabilities separately. A new curve without those conventions cannot support a quantitative comparison.

To add a new observable, first derive its measure and normalization, test an analytic or independent reference, expose it through the Wasm facade, then add a URL state and a labeled plot. To change the gravitational model, keep the sheet's mass bookkeeping independent from the trajectory generator. This separation makes the continuous-sheet estimator useful for other forward models without treating a different trajectory as an LPT result.


## Reusing the cosmology and diagnostic policies

The physical initial-spectrum module is independent of the trajectory and geometric modules. `cosmological::gaussian_hat` returns grid FFT coefficients with an explicit physical box, $\sigma_8$ normalization, initial Gaussian filter, integer cutoff and early-normalized growth conversion. It keys Gaussian draws by integer mode so refinement preserves the same realization. A project can instead supply a verified tabulated spectrum while retaining the same mode-pairing and sheet measurement conventions.

`nbody::evolve_cosmology` accepts a `Cosmology`, state, optional tangent direction and an orientation policy. With `allow_crossing=true`, it records the first crossed drift bracket and continues the discrete evolution; with `false`, it returns an error. The strict `evolve_eds` wrapper preserves the original pre-crossing API. The orientation policy is separate from gravity and observation: it controls validity reporting, not the mass sign or force. All parameter derivatives currently hold cosmology and clocks fixed.

The checked `laboratory::run_json` facade accepts exported manifests as well as plain requests. Its `request` field is the executed numerical specification, independent of camera angle and selected panel. The appendix's lower-level examples deliberately expose more responsibility: callers must enforce conservative input bandwidth, compatible meshes, finite geometry and measured conservation themselves. Reuse of an exact overlap routine establishes exact integration of a supplied affine element; it does not certify the supplied trajectories.

## Hybrid WebGPU observation backend {#sec-gpu-backend}

The optional compute backend evaluates the continuous fixed-mass sheet modes and their analytic position directions. Rust/Wasm constructs the initial Fourier field and integrates cosmological growth. Spectral nLPT construction and exact geometric deposition can also run on GPU, as described in @sec-gpu-lpt and @sec-gpu-exact-deposit. PDFs, gridded spectra and physical-unit finalization use Rust f64 arithmetic. PM trajectories can use either the f64 CPU reference or the resident GPU solver described below. The continuous-mode estimator uses the same sheet connectivity and fixed simplex masses for either trajectory source.

The prepared-run boundary retains the double-precision trajectory and tangent arrays. A GPU failure therefore reuses the prepared CPU state rather than repeating the physical calculation. Finalization uses the same Rust power normalization and unit conversion as the synchronous facade. The boundary is exposed by {{< src laboratory::prepare >}} and {{< src laboratory::PreparedLabRun >}}, and its compatibility and selective-recovery contracts are pinned by {{< test prepared_run_finishes_identically_and_validates_direct_channels "prepared-run contract" >}}.

| Stage | Arithmetic and execution |
|---|---|
| Initial Fourier conditions and cosmological growth | Rust/Wasm reference |
| nLPT spatial sources, displacements and tensors | Rust FFT reference or validated GPU FFT; f64 time factors and trajectory assembly |
| Cosmological PM trajectory and tangent | Rust f64 reference or validated resident GPU f32 solver |
| Exact density | CPU f64 clipping or validated GPU f32 cell-local clipping and compensated accumulation |
| PDFs and gridded power | Rust f64 statistics and FFT on f32 density fields |
| Continuous LPT/PM modes and analytic JVPs | Optional WGSL f32 kernel; CPU reference remains available |
| Weak LPT mode recovery | Compensated GPU analytic observer, then retained CPU f64 reference when required |
| Centered finite difference | Optional compensated GPU endpoint observer; cached CPU f64 reference and recovery |
| Power, derivative and physical units | Rust f64 finalization |

For a fixed-mass simplex, the kernel evaluates the barycentric exponential divided difference and its repeated-knot derivative from @eq-simplex-fourier and @eq-amplitude-jvp. It retains periodic lifts and the same two-triangle or six-tetrahedron connectivity. The port adapts the stable local Taylor/Newton strategy from the MIT-licensed [Hopf–Cole direct kernel](https://github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology/blob/3a3a13b9ba817c5b4f8f9f26314715845e13d4ad/app/js/gpu/direct.js). The [reuse manifest](../app/js/gpu/reuse-manifest.json) records original paths and hashes. Contributions are accumulated with an explicit reduction order and numerical diagnostics; no magnitude guard silently removes an element.

Displacements $\boldsymbol\psi=\boldsymbol x-\boldsymbol q$ are extracted in CPU f64 before conversion into packed f32 arrays. Integer lattice coordinates reconstruct the undeformed geometry. Only the exponential phase is reduced modulo $2\pi$; phase gaps in divided-difference denominators retain their full values. This distinction is necessary for both the primal integral and signed tangent coefficients. The four displacement/direction arrays occupy 16 MiB at $64^3$, before partial sums, staging and the retained CPU state.

The first backend covers 2D and 3D, including supported non-power-of-two lattices. One-dimensional requests use the CPU route. GPU resource refusal never changes the requested lattice, force mesh, observation mesh, bandwidth or epoch. A persistent numerical worker serializes requests, yields between bounded GPU submissions, discards obsolete generations, and releases owned buffers. During synchronous Rust preparation or CPU mode work, cancellation recreates the worker; during asynchronous GPU work it waits for submitted work and acknowledges cleanup.

### Precision, validation and reproduction

The portable [WGSL floating-point contract](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#floating-point-types) supplies f32 rather than an f64 path. The [GPU self-check](../app/gpu-test.html) compares primal and JVP components with independently converged barycentric quadrature. The complete-request harness separately compares full-f64 Rust inputs, f64 kernels on quantized inputs, and GPU arithmetic. Its comparison target is $|\Delta F|\le10^{-6}+10^{-4}|F_{\rm ref}|$ component by component, with the same target for the JVP. This absolute floor makes cancellation-dominated modes interpretable; it does not assert uniform relative accuracy for arbitrarily weak modes.

The existing amplitude derivative gate remains $|\partial_A P-P_{\rm FD}|/\max(|\partial_A P|,10^{-9})\le10^{-5}$ in internal unit-box units, at $h=10^{-4}$. The centered finite difference uses the compensated endpoint kernel in @sec-gpu-fd when its device check passes; it retains the f64 CPU reference and recovery route. Ordinary independently reduced f32 endpoint powers are insufficient for this check. When an LPT mode exceeds the gate, its value and analytic tangent are first recomputed together with compensated GPU arithmetic. Any remaining failure uses the CPU f64 reference; PM channels and passing LPT modes can remain on GPU. The manifest records the executed backend of each mode. This recovery is a numerical precision policy, independent of the shell-crossing caution.

CPU is the default. Selecting GPU attempts the accelerated observer and reports resource, capability or numerical fallback. Automatic selection remains on CPU until a device/workload policy is supported by accuracy and end-to-end measurements. Rendering uses the existing Canvas2D/SVG tier independently. Device limits, adapter metadata when exposed, shader hashes, reduction layout, stage durations and recovery decisions accompany the numerical results. Cross-device GPU replay uses stated tolerances rather than bitwise equality.

Run the independent kernel, complete cosmological requests, worker failure checks and repeated browser timings with:

```sh
make test
make test-wasm
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --full --output gpu-checks.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --benchmark --output gpu-benchmark.json
python3 scripts/profile_native_stages.py --dim 3 --repeats 3 --output native-profile.json
```

The browser runner requires Chrome (or `CHROME_PATH`) and has no npm dependencies. A missing adapter is reported as a skip; `--require-gpu` makes that a failing requirement. Normal hosted CI runs the native, Wasm and worker contracts, while GPU checks require a GPU-capable runner. See the [implementation plan](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-backend-plan.md) and [measurement record](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-results.md) for the tested requests and device-specific limits.

The independently checked extensions below retain selective CPU recovery for refused or numerically unsuccessful stages. The [optimization validation record](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-optimization-results.md) separates raw-field comparisons, full-request recovery and measured timings.

## Resident cosmological PM evolution {#sec-gpu-pm}

The resident stage carries unwrapped positions, canonical momenta, and their initial-amplitude directions through the same discrete cosmological PM equations as the CPU solver. The initial four-order growing state and the cosmological kick/drift integrals are supplied by Rust. For $\boldsymbol p=a^3 E(a)\,d\boldsymbol x/da$, each step uses the two half-kicks and full drift from @eq-kdk-integrals; only the numerical arithmetic changes to f32. The deferred boundary retains the f64 initial state until a successful GPU completion, so an allocation, validation, or execution failure can recover without rebuilding the initial realization. See {{< src laboratory::PendingLabRun >}} and the retained-state test {{< test pending_run_reuses_common_state_after_gpu_validation_failure "PM fallback contract" >}}.

The state buffer evolves $\boldsymbol\psi=\boldsymbol x-\boldsymbol q$, with subtraction performed in f64 before upload by {{< src laboratory::PendingLabRun::pm_displacement >}}. Force interpolation combines the integer lattice-to-force-grid quotient and remainder with $\boldsymbol\psi$, rather than rounding a small displacement into an absolute f32 position first. This matters for derivatives near CIC cell boundaries, where a change in interpolation branch can alter the JVP even when primal positions are close. Absolute f32 positions are materialized for orientation checks and exact observations. The reference harness separately reconstructs $\boldsymbol q+\operatorname{f32}(\boldsymbol\psi)$ in f64 to measure input quantization. A weak-mode packing test checks this distinction {{< test pm_displacement_packing_preserves_weak_modes_and_has_quantized_cpu_oracle "displacement precision" >}}.

Each force evaluation performs CIC deposition of both density and its direction, forward transforms, the derivative-safe spectral Poisson operation, inverse transforms, and CIC interpolation back to the particles. The gather direction includes the derivative of its interpolation weights as well as the force-field direction. Masses, cosmology, force mesh and clock schedule are held fixed. Thus the PM JVP differentiates the implemented discrete solver, including both CIC operations; it is not a cosmological-parameter gradient or an adjoint. The CPU equations and their independent finite-difference tests remain in @sec-pm.

The FFT is a Stockham radix-2 complex transform adapted from the pinned MIT [Hopf–Cole implementation](https://github.com/yipihey/hopf-cole-cosmology/blob/3a3a13b9ba817c5b4f8f9f26314715845e13d4ad/app/js/gpu/fft3d.js). It preserves last-axis-fast storage, the forward sign, and inverse normalization. The force denominator retains Nyquist contributions to $|\boldsymbol k|^2$, while odd derivatives use the zeroed Nyquist component from {{< src grid::Grid::kd >}}. A non-power-of-two force mesh retains CPU PM with an explicit reason; the requested lattice and observation grid are unchanged.

CIC deposition uses integer atomics to build per-node lists of particle contributions. One invocation sums the list for each node in floating point. This avoids fixed-point mass quantization and conflicting floating writes, but insertion order can depend on device scheduling, so cross-device and repeated-run agreement is assessed with tolerances. These CIC fields are force inputs. Displayed sheet density uses the separate exact geometric overlap observer, with the same positive-stream-mass accounting, PDF weighting and smoothing conventions; it can use CPU or GPU clipping.

### Drift orientation and precision

Every drift evaluates the determinant polynomial on each interval, triangle or Kuhn tetrahedron at both endpoints and at all interior stationary points. A flag records nonfinite polynomial arithmetic. When the GPU candidate is at most $10^{-3}$, or is invalid, Rust recomputes the complete drift minimum in f64 from the f32 endpoints actually evolved. The threshold is a recheck policy, not a universal error bound. Initial orientation is checked for both the original f64 and quantized f32 initial sheet. The first failed drift is retained as a bracket, and evolution continues with the shell-crossing caution. The CPU extrema calculation is exposed by {{< src nbody::minimum_drift_jacobian >}}, with an interior-fold test {{< test drift_guard_detects_interior_fold_with_positive_endpoint_jacobians "continuous drift extrema" >}} and boundary-bracket test {{< test pending_gpu_result_records_first_verified_drift_bracket "crossing bracket" >}}.

PM state, tangents, CIC sums and FFT fields use f32; Rust clocks are rounded to f32 when uploaded. Exact observation integration uses its separately recorded CPU or GPU arithmetic; final power and unit conversion remain CPU f64. The per-device gate compares FFT modes, a direct-DFT CIC force/JVP reference, and complete PM states against Rust with both original and quantized initial inputs. A separate full suite checks observation statistics, crossings, resource refusal and cancellation. The measured requests, tolerances, source hashes and timings are recorded in [the resident-backend validation record](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-pm-results.md).

```sh
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --resident --output resident-checks.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --resident-benchmark --output resident-benchmark.json
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Inspect trajectory and observation provenance"}
Select GPU and inspect the PM evolution entry together with the continuous-mode precision table. The two stages can recover independently. The exported manifest retains device checks, clocks' physical request, shader hashes, precision, timings and fallback reasons.

{{< lab "v=3&dim=3&n=32&epoch=scaleFactor&a=0.25&steps=32&mesh=32&force=32&backend=gpu&view=gradient" "Resident PM and continuous-mode response" >}}
:::


## Centered finite differences on GPU {#sec-gpu-fd}

The amplitude check evaluates two actual perturbed LPT sheets at fixed epoch,
$\boldsymbol x_\pm=\boldsymbol x(A\pm h)$ with $h=10^{-4}$. It does not reuse the
analytic JVP as an approximation to these endpoint values. The value-only
continuous simplex integral from @eq-simplex-fourier gives $F_\pm$; the check is

$$
P_{\rm FD}=\frac{|F_+|^2-|F_-|^2}{2h}
=\frac{\operatorname{Re}[(F_+-F_-)\overline{(F_++F_-)}]}{2h}.
$$ {#eq-gpu-centered-fd}

Directly subtracting independently rounded endpoint amplitudes amplifies their
absolute errors by $1/h$. The GPU instead evaluates the same endpoint
difference through a continuous path between the retained geometries. Write
$\boldsymbol x_j(\theta)=\boldsymbol c_j+\theta\boldsymbol b_j$, where
$\boldsymbol c_j=(\boldsymbol x_{+,j}+\boldsymbol x_{-,j})/2$ and
$\boldsymbol b_j=(\boldsymbol x_{+,j}-\boldsymbol x_{-,j})/2$.
Then

$$
\Delta F=F_+-F_-=\int_{-1}^{1}\frac{dF(\theta)}{d\theta}\,d\theta.
$$ {#eq-gpu-endpoint-path}

For a simplex contribution $F_T=w_T\exp[s_0,\ldots,s_d]$ with
$s_j=-2\pi i\boldsymbol m\cdot\boldsymbol x_j(\theta)$, differentiation gives

$$
\frac{dF_T}{d\theta}=w_T\sum_{j=0}^{d}
(-2\pi i\boldsymbol m\cdot\boldsymbol b_j)
\exp[s_0,\ldots,s_d,s_j].
$$ {#eq-gpu-endpoint-path-derivative}

These repeated-knot integrals use the actual endpoint gaps. The path is an
integration device, rather than an intermediate LPT trajectory; the analytic
LPT amplitude direction is not supplied to this observer. Three-point
Gauss–Legendre quadrature uses nodes $0,\pm\sqrt{3/5}$ and weights
$8/9,5/9,5/9$ on $[-1,1]$. For a unit-total-mass sheet define
$M=\pi\max_T\max_j|\boldsymbol m\cdot(\boldsymbol x_{+,j}-\boldsymbol x_{-,j})|$.
The [Gauss remainder formula](https://dlmf.nist.gov/3.5.E19), applied separately
to the real and imaginary parts, bounds the quadrature error by
$|\epsilon_{\Delta F}|\le\sqrt{2}M^7/15750$.
Since $|F_++F_-|\le2$, the induced power-derivative error is at most
$\sqrt{2}M^7/(15750h)$.
The host checks the conservative bound
$M\le\pi\|\boldsymbol m\|_1\max_{j,a}|x_{+,j,a}-x_{-,j,a}|\le0.005$;
otherwise this stage recovers on CPU. At the limit and $h=10^{-4}$, the
quadrature contribution is below $7.1\times10^{-17}$ in internal units.
This is a truncation bound, not a bound on GPU roundoff.

The endpoint sum and independently accumulated $\Delta F$ return to host f64
for @eq-gpu-centered-fd. The physical volume factor is applied later by the
same Rust finalizer as for the analytic derivative.

Rust retains both f64 endpoint geometries. For each displacement component it
packs $\psi_{\rm hi}=\operatorname{f32}(x_\pm-q)$ and
$\psi_{\rm lo}=\operatorname{f32}[(x_\pm-q)-\psi_{\rm hi}]$.
Integer lattice coordinates supply $q$ without prematurely rounding the sum
$q+\psi$ into an absolute f32 position. The typed getters and externally
supplied finite-difference finalizer are exposed by
{{< src laboratory::PreparedLabRun::finite_difference_plus_hi >}} and
{{< src laboratory::PreparedLabRun::finish_with_finite_difference >}};
{{< test prepared_run_finishes_identically_and_validates_direct_channels "endpoint packing and finalization" >}}
checks reconstruction, output compatibility and invalid-channel rejection.
The external finalizer consumes the supplied values directly, without
invoking the CPU endpoint observer. The CPU series evaluator also uses a tail
bound: a vanishing odd coefficient in a symmetric knot set does not justify
omitting later even coefficients. This case is covered by
{{< test symmetric_repeated_knots_do_not_stop_at_zero_odd_terms "symmetric-knot series regression" >}}.

The WGSL evaluator carries high/low pairs through phase construction,
exponential divided differences and fixed-order reductions. It uses explicit
rounding barriers and split-product residuals, with reduced-phase polynomials
for the complex exponential and the same periodic simplex lifts and fixed
masses as the other continuous observer. Phase spans below 3 radians use a factorial-tail rule to select the retained normalized series terms, capped at 40; wider separated knots use divided differences. Both
endpoint sheets retain their own geometry, including orientation reversals.
The four vec4 input arrays occupy 16 MiB at $64^3$. For the six observed modes,
per-cell complex plus/minus/delta expansions occupy another 72 MiB. Separate passes
reduce each 32-cell block and then all blocks in a fixed order, with one sum
owner per block or mode. Endpoint evaluation, delta evaluation and chunk
reduction are separate completed submissions before the next stage consumes
their storage. These fields, partials and readback buffers are checked
against the device and per-run allocation limits.

For $c$ phase knots, define $\beta_j=-2\pi(\phi_j-\bar\phi)$ and the
complete homogeneous coefficients by
$\prod_j(1-\beta_j t)^{-1}=\sum_{m\ge0}h_m t^m$.
If $e_r$ are the elementary symmetric coefficients of the $\beta_j$, the
normalized coefficients $g_m=h_m/(m+c-1)!$ obey

$$
g_m=\sum_{r=1}^{\min(m,c)}
\frac{(-1)^{r-1}e_r g_{m-r}}
{\prod_{s=0}^{r-1}(m+c-1-s)},\qquad
 g_0=\frac{1}{(c-1)!}.
$$ {#eq-gpu-normalized-series}

The local integral is $e^{-2\pi i\bar\phi}\sum_m i^m g_m$.
The repeated-node derivative requires five knots in 3D and five lagged
coefficients; the
[WGSL implementation](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/app/js/gpu/finite-difference.js)
keeps them in registers. A phase span below 3 radians gives
$R=\sum_j|\beta_j|\le7.5$ for at most five knots, and
$|h_m|\le R^m$ bounds the omitted factorial tail after 40 terms below
$10^{-17}g_0$. The optimized kernel specializes each knot count and selects the shortest retained order $K\le40$ satisfying a conservative tail estimate. For $R<K+c+1$, the exact-arithmetic bound is

$$
\left|\sum_{m>K}i^m g_m\right|\le
\frac{R^{K+1}}{(K+c)!}\frac{1}{1-R/(K+c+1)}.
$$ {#eq-gpu-adaptive-tail}

The GPU inflates the computed radius and ratio before comparison with $5\times10^{-18}g_0$; device and retained-f64 checks still determine acceptance of its rounded arithmetic. A zero individual coefficient never ends the series. Projected midpoint displacements and endpoint gaps are computed once per cell vertex and reused at all three Gauss nodes. The completed submission boundaries and 32-cell reduction layout are retained. Normalization avoids separately constructing large $h_m$ and
very small inverse factorials. Independent arithmetic, repeated-knot and
complete-request fixtures check the resulting observer.

High/low arithmetic is a compensated f32 implementation, rather than native
f64. The [WGSL evaluation contract](https://www.w3.org/TR/WGSL/#floating-point-evaluation)
permits transformations whose behavior depends on the compiler and adapter.
Each acquired device must therefore pass independent endpoint and
finite-difference fixtures before this stage is enabled. Complete-request
checks separately compare the GPU result with retained Rust f64 endpoint
integrals, including weak modes. The acceptance target is
$|P_{\rm FD,GPU}-P_{\rm FD,CPU}|/\max(|P_{\rm FD,CPU}|,10^{-9})\le10^{-5}$
in internal units. This fixture budget is distinct from the unchanged
analytic-derivative gate.

Capability, resource, validation or execution failures recover the cached
f64 CPU finite difference without discarding a completed PM trajectory or
passing direct channels. If the derivative gate still fails after f64 LPT
mode recovery, the worker checks again using CPU finite differences before
requiring complete CPU direct-mode recovery. The manifest records FD
precision, step, shader hashes, device validation, timings and any recovery
reason separately from PM and analytic channels. Submitted endpoint batches
are cancellable with the same owned-buffer cleanup contract as the other
GPU stages. One-dimensional requests and automatic backend selection retain
CPU execution.

```sh
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --fd --output fd-checks.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --fd-benchmark --output fd-benchmark.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --fd-repeat --output fd-repeat.json
```

See the [finite-difference validation record](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-fd-results.md)
for requests, observed discrepancies, measured timing scopes and device limits.

## Spectral nLPT construction on GPU {#sec-gpu-lpt}

Spatial nLPT fields depend on the initial modes and their polynomial source recursion, while cosmological time factors depend on the background and epoch. The GPU boundary preserves this separation. Rust generates the actual initial Fourier coefficients, including the physical spectrum normalization and filters. The GPU builds every unmerged longitudinal and transverse term through fourth order from its parent gradient tensors, then returns displacements, gradients and scalar or curl sources. Rust installs these fields, applies the existing Einstein–de Sitter merging policy where appropriate, and evaluates the same f64 growth functions and initial-amplitude directions.

The source operators are the $\mu_2$, $\mu_3$ and curl contractions used by the CPU recurrence. Their FFT solves retain the last-axis-fast layout, forward sign, inverse $1/N$ normalization, full $|\boldsymbol k|^2$ denominator and derivative-safe Nyquist convention. A longitudinal solve therefore uses the full Laplacian denominator with the zeroed odd derivative $k_a^{\rm D}$ in its numerator; transverse solves preserve the curl orientation. Changing the arithmetic backend does not change the initial realization, input bandwidth, time normalization, or perturbative coefficients.

The boundary {{< src gpu_lpt::GpuLptSeed >}} constructs the initial Fourier field without building a hidden CPU nLPT reference. Its explicitly requested raw-field oracle supports numerical comparisons. The constructor {{< src lpt::Lpt::from_packed_fields >}} rejects malformed or nonfinite payloads before installing them. Tests reconstruct the CPU raw terms through this boundary and compare all four orders, EdS and $\Lambda$CDM time factors, trajectories, Jacobians and actual amplitude directions; rejected payloads leave the seed usable {{< test raw_lpt_boundary_preserves_growth_merge_and_actual_amplitude_direction "raw nLPT boundary" >}}.

The GPU spectral path requires a power-of-two Lagrangian lattice in 2D or 3D. Every acquired device first checks plane waves along each axis and an independent quadratic two-wave solution. Complete fixtures then compare every raw field with Rust. The device requests adapter-supported storage/buffer limits up to 512 MiB, following the [WebGPU limits contract](https://www.w3.org/TR/webgpu/#limits). The 64³ raw fourth-order payload exceeds the portable 128 MiB storage-binding default, so a device with only that limit recovers on CPU. Complete per-stage allocations still have a separate 512 MiB cap. A resource, finite-value, validation or readback failure retains the requested experiment and rebuilds nLPT with the CPU algorithm. Initial-condition generation and cosmological growth integration remain CPU stages. This is a spatial-field backend, rather than a new physical approximation.

## Exact geometric deposition on GPU {#sec-gpu-exact-deposit}

For the represented affine sheet, a cell receives the fixed positive simplex mass multiplied by the fraction of its Eulerian image intersecting that cell. The observer clips a triangle or tetrahedron against each candidate Cartesian cell, measures the intersection, and accumulates its mass according to @eq-exact-deposition. It uses the same periodic lifts and Kuhn connectivity as Rust. Candidate bounding boxes limit the cells visited; no quadrature samples, virtual particles, or shot-noise subtraction enter this estimator.

The GPU translates and scales each clipping problem into the local cell $[0,1]^d$. This avoids forming small intersection volumes by subtracting distant absolute coordinates. Each simplex writes positive f32 contribution records. Integer atomic links assign these records to cells; one invocation owns each cell's Kahan-compensated floating sum. The resulting density is $\rho/\bar\rho$, so its **mean**, rather than its sum, must be one. Insertion order can vary with GPU scheduling, and reproduction uses stated component budgets rather than bitwise equality.

The geometric port adapts the pinned Hopf–Cole triangle clipper and the R3D-style tetrahedron graph clipper. It replaces upstream fixed-point deposition with floating contribution records and explicit capacity accounting. Overflow, malformed graph walks, nonfinite measures and poorly conditioned slivers produce a failed GPU stage and CPU recovery. Exactly degenerate elements follow the represented-sheet convention of the CPU observer; global conservation is checked before accepting a laboratory density. No missing mass is hidden by renormalization.

The external-density boundary {{< src laboratory::LabSession::finish_gpu_pm_observed >}} checks field length, finite nonnegative entries and a unit mean within $10^{-6}$ before caching or computing statistics. Invalid density can therefore recover CPU observation without repeating a successful GPU trajectory. Native tests pin exact-oracle compatibility, rejection, recovery and provenance partitioning {{< test external_density_finish_matches_exact_reference_and_rejects_invalid_mass_without_poisoning_cache "external density contract" >}}. Device checks include identity, periodic translation, folds, seam streams and thin-element refusal; complete requests separately compare cell fields, spectra and PDF summaries with the CPU reference.

The clipping algorithm integrates the affine sheet geometrically, but its GPU geometry and accumulation use f32. The CPU f64 clipper remains the accuracy reference. This arithmetic qualification is separate from exact integration of the represented element and from the validity of the supplied LPT trajectory after shell crossing.

## Compensated analytic recovery and retained work {#sec-gpu-retained-work}

Weak Fourier modes can result from cancellation between large simplex contributions. The ordinary f32 observer may then fail the amplitude-derivative gate even when its absolute error is small. The recovery observer uses high/low f32 expansions of the actual retained f64 displacement and **analytic** amplitude direction. It evaluates the same exponential divided differences and repeated-node JVP in @eq-amplitude-jvp with compensated phase, integral and reduction arithmetic. It supplies no endpoint finite difference as an analytic derivative. The endpoint-path check in @sec-gpu-fd remains independent.

Only modes requiring recovery need this more expensive arithmetic. Their value and tangent are replaced together, the unchanged per-mode gate is evaluated again, and any remaining failures use CPU f64 integration. The CPU simplex JVP now reuses a fixed-size knot workspace and retained divided-difference storage across elements, avoiding repeated heap allocations while preserving signed directions and repeated-knot limits. The [closed repeated-knot unit regression](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/core/src/tangent.rs#:~:text=fn%20repeated_knot_workspace_matches_closed_form_without_capacity_growth) also checks that workspace capacity remains stable. Independent centered derivatives check the simplex observer {{< test simplex_jvp_mass_degeneracies_translation_and_p1_finite_difference "simplex JVP" >}}.

A persistent {{< src laboratory::LabSession >}} retains one compatible entry at each of four levels: initial Fourier/nLPT fields, prepared geometry and validity diagnostics, completed PM evolution, and unsmoothed density/spectrum observations. The combined retention budget is 256 MiB. Entries are keyed by the complete physical input and executed precision source. Epoch and force/timestep changes invalidate dependent work; changing the LPT output order can reuse the common fourth-order PM initialization; changing the observation mesh reuses the completed PM state and rebuilds deposition; changing only observation smoothing reuses the unsmoothed observations. Validation diagnostics travel with the retained geometry rather than being inferred from a previous plot.

CPU/GPU initialization, f64/f32 PM arithmetic and CPU/GPU deposition have distinct keys. Failed or nonconserved external fields cannot poison a later hit. A fresh PM evolution invalidates the previous raw observations, and newly supplied density fields are consumed rather than replaced with a previous entry. Reusing a trajectory across observation-mesh changes retains its original state and crossing diagnostics {{< test cached_pm_positions_rebuild_new_mesh_and_never_reuse_stale_external_deposits "PM observation reuse" >}}. An oversized entry is skipped, with its reason and retained bytes recorded. A cache is local to the worker and can be discarded on cancellation during synchronous Rust work; exported manifests reproduce the experiment independently of its cache history. Cache reuse tests compare changed observation controls with fresh computations and exercise physical invalidation {{< test lab_session_reuses_physical_trajectory_and_raw_observations_with_exact_keys "session cache contract" >}}.

```sh
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --optimization-self --output optimization-self.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --optimizations --output optimization-checks.json
node scripts/test_gpu.mjs --require-gpu --optimization-benchmark --output optimization-benchmark.json
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Inspect the complete execution path"}
Use a radix lattice and force mesh, inspect nLPT construction, PM evolution, exact deposition, analytic recovery and cache status, then change observation smoothing. Export the manifest to retain every stage's executed arithmetic, device checks, kernel hashes and fallback reason. A crossed result remains visible with its existing validity caution.

{{< lab "v=3&backend=gpu&dim=3&n=32&mesh=32&force=32&steps=32&epoch=scaleFactor&a=0.25&ic=waves&view=gradient" "Open the GPU stage laboratory" >}}
:::

The recorded complete cold-request medians are 3,207.7 to 1,056.4 ms at $32^3$ and 21,934.6 to 7,342.0 ms at $64^3$, comparing CPU spatial nLPT/clipping/analytic recovery with the enabled GPU additions. Both policies use the optimized PM and FD kernels. All timed mass, derivative and field budgets pass. The [measurement record](https://github.com/yipihey/precrossedsheet/blob/main/docs/webgpu-optimization-results.md) gives ranges, device details and complete source fingerprints. A smoothing-only $32^3$ cache hit has a 269.7 ms median; at $64^3$, the bounded cache retains initial fields and geometry but recomputes PM and deposition. These results characterize the measured requests and adapter.
